_comments: THE HOURLY ACTIVITY-SYNC ACTION. Fired by the ScheduledJob under metadata/scheduled-jobs/.
DriverClass is a ClassFactory key, not a display name: @RegisterClass(BaseAction,
resolves to, and LoadSyncActivitiesAction() in the server bootstrap is what keeps that
registration from being tree-shaken away. Get either wrong and the action exists in metadata,
is scheduled, fires on time, and does nothing — with no error anywhere.
Downstream apps do not wrap this. They register a BaseActivitySyncExtension (e.g.
Sales.DealLinker) which the engine runs inside the write transaction.
SAFE TO SHIP Active: Graph providers refuse live fetch until an Exchange Application Access
Policy exists, so an hourly run against a Microsoft365 connection writes nothing until a
deployment opts in. A host with no ActivitySyncConnection reports NO_CONNECTIONS.
No sync block — the release push writes that back. primaryKey from uuidgen.

fields.Name: Sync Activities
fields.Description: Pull messages and calendar items for every Active-or-Error activity-sync connection and file the relevant ones as Activities. Downstream apps enrich in-stream via ActivitySyncExtension; they do not own this trigger. Idempotent: re-running over the same window writes nothing new.

fields.Name: Limit
fields.Description: How many items to pull per mailbox per surface per run. MJ's GetMessages contract has no date filter, so a run fetches the most recent N and discards what it has already seen — anything older than the Nth newest message since the last run is missed and never retried.
Every attempted connection completed with no failed items.
At least one connection was attempted and at least one item or surface failed.
The connection list loaded successfully and was empty. Not used when the list failed to load.
The run failed before any connection was attempted (including a failed connection list load), or threw.

fields.Name: Common.LogActivity
fields.Description: Writes one Activity plus its ActivityLink rows to the unified timeline through the shared ActivityWriter (one writer, two entry points — this is the manual/declarative one). Bind AfterCreate/AfterUpdate on any entity to this action and the record's lifecycle appears on the person's or organization's timeline with no code in the consuming app. Bind RecordData with ValueType 'Entity Object Data' — NEVER 'Entity Object', which serializes to {} silently. Idempotency: pass EventKey for one-per-record events (AfterCreate) so a durable retry cannot double-log; leave it off when every firing should log. Sync extensions do NOT run on this path — they fire on ingest, not on a record being logged.

fields.Name: TypeCode
fields.Description: ActivityType.Code of the entry (e.g. SystemEvent, Note). Resolved by code so renaming a type never breaks bindings.

fields.Name: Title
fields.Description: One-line card title for the timeline entry.

fields.Name: Description
fields.Description: Optional notes / excerpt. May carry personal data — not logged.

fields.Name: StartedAt
fields.Description: Timeline sort key (Date or ISO string). Defaults to now.

fields.Name: EndedAt
fields.Description: End of a meeting/call. Must be on or after StartedAt.

fields.Name: Direction
fields.Description: Inbound, Outbound or Internal. Defaults to Internal.

fields.Name: Status
fields.Description: Logged, Scheduled, Completed, Cancelled or Failed. Defaults to Logged.

fields.Name: Visibility
fields.Description: Internal or Private. Defaults to Internal — the manual-log default; the sync engine's Private is for mail nobody chose to share.

fields.Name: Source
fields.Description: Manual or System. Defaults to Manual. 'Integration' belongs to the sync engine's entry point and is refused here.

fields.Name: Location
fields.Description: Meeting place as text.

fields.Name: Details
fields.Description: JSON extras that are not query predicates. Stringified into Activity.Details. Not logged.

fields.Name: EntityName
fields.Description: MJ entity name of the record this activity is about. With RecordID (or RecordData.ID) it becomes a leading Regarding link.

fields.Name: RecordID
fields.Description: The subject record's id. Optional when RecordData carries ID.

fields.Name: RecordData
fields.Description: The subject record as a PLAIN object. In an Entity Action binding use ValueType 'Entity Object Data' — never 'Entity Object', which serializes to {} silently. Carries whole records — never logged.

fields.Name: LinkFields
fields.Description: Declarative link routing: [{ Field, EntityName, Role }] — reads Field from RecordData and links that record. This is what routes a binding on any entity to the People/Organizations rows it references. Null FKs are skipped.

fields.Name: Links
fields.Description: Extra explicit links: [{ Role, EntityName, RecordID }] or [{ Role, IdentityKind, IdentityValue }]. May carry identity values — not logged.

fields.Name: SourceSystem
fields.Description: Idempotency namespace, paired with ExternalID. Required when ExternalID is set.

fields.Name: ExternalID
fields.Description: Idempotency key within SourceSystem. A repeat write with the same pair is a no-op reporting AlreadyPresent.

fields.Name: EventKey
fields.Description: Makes a binding idempotent per record: ExternalID becomes EntityName|RecordID|EventKey and SourceSystem defaults to 'EntityAction'. Use for one-per-record events (AfterCreate); leave off when every firing should log.

fields.Name: ActivityID
fields.Description: ID of the written (or already-present) activity.

fields.Name: AlreadyPresent
fields.Description: True when the SourceSystem/ExternalID pair already existed and nothing was written.
The activity and its links were written.
An activity with this SourceSystem/ExternalID already exists; nothing was written.
The inputs were invalid; the message lists every problem.
The write failed; the transaction rolled back and the message carries the issues.
